_comment: Explanations written for this app (the released tests publish only the answer key). Keyed by question ID from src/data/deck.json.
naep-m016501: 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5. Together, 8 and 12 only give 2³ × 3 = 24, so the third number has to bring the factor 5 without adding anything that 120 doesn't have. 15 = 3 × 5 works. 16, 24, 32 and 48 have no factor of 5, so their LCM with 8 and 12 can't be 120.
naep-m025101: From 1:00 to 2:30 is 90 minutes, a little more than three 28-minute doubling periods (84 minutes). About 5 million doubled three times: 5 → 10 → 20 → 40 million, and a bit more by 2:30. Of the choices, 40 million is closest.
naep-m059601: Pick an easy example: n = 2 leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 7. Then 2n + 1 = 5, which leaves a remainder of 5. In general n = 7k + 2, so 2n + 1 = 14k + 5, and 14k is a multiple of 7.
naep-m059001: Tens digit 4 → 5 adds 10. Thousands digit 7 → 6 subtracts 1,000. Net change: +10 − 1,000 = −990. (Check: 37,241 becomes 36,251, which is 990 less.)
naep-m061201: There are 1,200 − 300 = 900 nonvegetarians. Nonvegetarians to vegetarians is 900 to 300, which simplifies to 3 to 1. Watch the order: the question asks for nonvegetarians first.
naep-m023801: Turn each fraction into a decimal: 1/50 = 0.02, 1/5 = 0.2, 1/4 = 0.25, 1/3 ≈ 0.33, 1/2 = 0.5. The closest to 0.52 is 0.5.
naep-m049101: 1 billion = 1,000,000,000 and 1 million = 1,000,000. 1,000,000,000 ÷ 1,000,000 = 1,000, so one billion is a thousand millions.
naep-m051901: 10% of 90 is 9, so the company grew by 9 employees: 90 + 9 = 99. Choice A (9) is only the increase, not the new total.
naep-m107601: Descending at twice the climbing rate means 2 × 66.8 = 133.6 feet per minute. In 30 minutes: 133.6 × 30 = 4,008 feet. Choice D (2,004) is what it would climb in 30 minutes.
naep-m051501: odd × odd is always odd (for example 3 × 5 = 15). The others fail: two consecutive integers include an even one, so their product is even; even + even + even is even; odd + odd is even; and three consecutive integers can add up to an even number (1 + 2 + 3 = 6).
naep-m164801: The ratio 6:5:2 has 6 + 5 + 2 = 13 parts. 78 ÷ 13 = 6 people per part. Adults are 2 parts: 2 × 6 = 12.
naep-m166101: Moving the decimal point one place to the left divides by 10, which gives 10% of the bill. Doubling that gives 20%. (Rounding to the nearest ten cents barely changes anything.)
naep-m086001: 1.08 × 10⁸ means moving the decimal point 8 places to the right: 1.08 → 108,000,000.
naep-m016801: "Length is 3 more than width" means L = W + 3. Solve for the width: W = L − 3. A common trap is to write L + 3, which reverses the relationship.
naep-m016901: The figures have 3, 5, 7, 9 dots, so each one adds 2. Figure n has 2n + 1 dots (check: figure 1 has 2(1) + 1 = 3). Figure 100 has 2(100) + 1 = 201.
naep-m095201: Add the two equations. The 2y and −2y cancel, leaving 2x = 20, so x = 10. (Then y = 3.5, and 10 + 7 = 17 checks.)
naep-m016001: 2x > 11 means x > 5.5. The smallest whole number greater than 5.5 is 6. Be careful: 5 doesn't work, because 2 × 5 = 10 is not greater than 11.
naep-m093301: Chaz is next to both Bridgitte and Diann, and Chaz is the only one next to Bridgitte, so Bridgitte must be in an end house. If Bridgitte is in #1: Chaz #2, Diann #3, Allen #4. If Bridgitte is in #4: Chaz #3, Diann #2, Allen #1. So house #2 could be Chaz or Diann.
naep-m111201: The pattern is the squares of the odd numbers: 1², 3², 5², 7², 9². The 6th number is 11² = 121.
naep-m111601: Test each rule against the table. y = 3x − 1 works for every row: 3(0) − 1 = −1, 3(1) − 1 = 2, 3(2) − 1 = 5, 3(3) − 1 = 8, 3(10) − 1 = 29. The other rules break on at least one row.
naep-m067401: The new y is 4(x + 2) = 4x + 8, which is the original 4x plus 8. Each increase of 1 in x adds 4 to y, so an increase of 2 adds 8.
naep-m047701: The examples show that the sum of the first n odd numbers is n²: 1 + 3 = 4 = 2², 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 = 3², and so on. 144 = 12², so it takes 12 odd numbers.
naep-m107101: Let Shawn sell s hot dogs. Carmen sold 3s, so s + 3s = 152. Then 4s = 152 and s = 38. Carmen sold 3 × 38 = 114. Choice B (38) is Shawn's total.
naep-m154101: In y = 800 − 50x, the tank starts with 800 gallons when x = 0, and every hour (x goes up 1) y goes down by 50. So the tank is emptying at 50 gallons per hour. 800 is the starting amount, not the rate.
naep-m154301: Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding a positive one, so a − b = a + (a positive) > 0. Check the others with a = 1, b = −5: ab = −5, b − a = −6, a + b = −4. With a = 5, b = −1, a + b = 4, so neither D nor E must be true.
naep-m151101: Substitute t = 400 into h = 73 + 2.5t: 2.5 × 400 = 1,000, and 73 + 1,000 = 1,073 centimeters.
naep-m093001: Order of operations: do the division and multiplication first. 15 ÷ 3 = 5 and 4 × 2 = 8. Then add and subtract left to right: 3 + 5 − 8 = 0.
naep-m016401: Put M at 0 on a number line. Then N is at 20, P at 32 and Q at 48. The midpoint of MN is at 10 and the midpoint of PQ is at 40. 40 − 10 = 30 cm.
naep-m016601: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 30 and 40. 30² + 40² = 900 + 1,600 = 2,500, and √2,500 = 50 inches. (It's a 3-4-5 triangle scaled up by 10.)
naep-m061301: Joining the midpoints of the sides of any quadrilateral always makes a parallelogram. Each side of the new figure is parallel to one of the original figure's diagonals. They aren't always rectangles, squares or rhombuses; that depends on the diagonals.
naep-m049701: A diameter is the longest segment that joins two points of a circle. BC is a chord that doesn't pass through the center, so it's shorter than the diameter AC.
naep-m052001: An exterior angle of 135° at C means the interior angle at C is 180° − 135° = 45°. The angles of a triangle add to 180°, so ∠ABC = 180° − 25° − 45° = 110°.
naep-m048001: This figure is an isosceles trapezoid. The parallel sides (the bases) are unequal, so the equal pair must be the other two sides. Only one pair of sides is parallel, so those equal sides are not parallel.
naep-m153401: Reflecting over the y-axis flips left and right: (x, y) becomes (−x, y). So (3, 7) becomes (−3, 7).
naep-m168401: A straight line can cross a circle in at most 2 points. A square has 4 sides, so the most is 4 × 2 = 8. A circle a little smaller than the square, sharing its center, crosses each side twice.
naep-m061601: Volume of a cylinder = πr²h. w = π(4²)(6) = 96π, x = π(3²)(8) = 72π, y = π(2²)(12) = 48π. So y < x < w.
naep-m024901: Dropping the water 1 foot removes 24 × 8 × 1 = 192 cubic feet. At 0.40 cubic foot per minute, that takes 192 ÷ 0.4 = 480 minutes, and 480 ÷ 60 = 8 hours.
naep-m176801: The smallest possible area is 15.5 × 11.5 = 178.25 and the largest is 16.5 × 12.5 = 206.25 square feet. The interval has to contain both. 179 to 206 misses both ends; 178 to 207 is the smallest choice that contains them.
naep-m110001: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width, so 390 = 2L + 2(75) = 2L + 150. Then 2L = 240 and L = 120 feet.
naep-m142501: This is a right trapezoid. The slanted 5 cm side and the 4 cm height form a right triangle, so its bottom leg is 3 cm (3-4-5). The bottom base is 8 + 3 = 11 cm. Area = ½ × (8 + 11) × 4 = 38 square centimeters.
naep-m143101: A clock face is 360° split into 12 hour marks, so each mark is 30°. At 10 o'clock the hands point at 10 and 12, which are 2 marks apart: 2 × 30° = 60°.
naep-m061401: One huge salary changes the highest salary, the range, the mean and the standard deviation a lot. The median is the middle value, and adding one value at the top moves the middle by at most one position. So the median stays about the same.
naep-m094801: Find the totals first: class A sold 10 × 4 = 40 boxes and class B sold 15 × 9 = 135 boxes. 175 boxes ÷ 25 students = 7. Averaging 4 and 9 to get 6½ is a trap, because the classes are different sizes.
naep-m070901: In a box-and-whisker plot, the right edge of the box is the upper quartile: 75% of the data is below it. The box ends at 33, so three-fourths of the cars got fewer than 33 miles per gallon.
naep-m017001: There are 15 + 11 = 26 students and 11 of them are boys. P(boy) = 11/26.
naep-m023501: 2 out of 25 dead is the same rate as x out of 500. 500 is 25 × 20, so x = 2 × 20 = 40.
naep-m107201: Books weigh 3, 5, 4 and 6 lb. All 4 single books work. All 6 pairs work (the heaviest pair is 5 + 6 = 11). Of the 4 groups of three, only 3 + 5 + 4 = 12 works. All four books weigh 18. Total: 4 + 6 + 1 = 11.
naep-m150701: The dog that changed weighed 31, the minimum, and it got lighter. The maximum, mode (88), quartiles and median all depend on the other dogs, so they don't move. Lowering one value always lowers the mean.
